pageInfo.subtitle: Master position shifting and fretboard mapping exercises to navigate the entire guitar neck with confidence.
pageInfo.heroDescription: One of the biggest barriers for intermediate guitarists is being stuck in one position. These exercises systematically develop your ability to navigate the entire fretboard, shift positions smoothly, and mentally map notes across all strings and frets.

items.text: Maintain thumb behind the neck as your anchor point
Use guide fingers to slide smoothly between positions
Keep eyes on the fretboard initially, then practice without looking
Learn note names on strings 6 and 5 first (root notes)
Use octave patterns to find notes on other strings
Practice naming notes while playing scales
Visualize scale shapes connecting across positions

exercises.title: Chromatic Position Shift
exercises.description: Play a chromatic pattern (1-2-3-4) starting at fret 1, then shift up one fret and repeat. Continue shifting up to fret 9 and back down. Focus on smooth transitions between positions with minimal pause.

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Use one-finger-per-fret technique. When shifting, let your hand glide as a unit. The shift should be quick and decisive, not gradual.

exercises.title: Octave Jumping Exercise
exercises.description: Play a note on the low E string, then immediately find the same note one octave higher using the octave shape (2 strings up, 2 frets forward). This builds your octave pattern awareness across the entire fretboard.

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Name each note as you play it. This octave pattern (2 strings up, 2 frets forward) works for strings 6-4 and 5-3. For strings 4-2 and 3-1, the upper note is 3 frets forward.

exercises.title: Three-Position Scale Run
exercises.description: Play the A minor pentatonic scale through three positions: Position 1 (frets 5-8), Position 2 (frets 7-10), Position 3 (frets 10-12). Connect them smoothly with guide finger slides.

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: The key to connecting positions is finding shared notes between shapes. Use your index or pinky as guide fingers to slide into new positions.

exercises.title: Note Name Drill - Low Strings
exercises.description: Play every natural note on strings 6 and 5, naming each note aloud as you play. Start at the open string and work up to the 12th fret. This builds the foundation for finding chord roots and scale positions anywhere on the neck.

notation.title: Natural Notes - String 6 (E)
notation.staveTitle: E F G A B C D E - String 6

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Say each note name out loud: E(0) F(1) G(3) A(5) B(7) C(8) D(10) E(12). Once comfortable, try random frets and name the notes.

exercises.title: One-String Scale
exercises.description: Play the C major scale entirely on string 6 from open position to the 12th fret. This forces you to visualize scale intervals linearly rather than relying on box patterns. Repeat on each string.

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Notice the pattern of whole and half steps on a single string: W-W-H-W-W-W-H. This approach reveals the scale structure clearly.

exercises.title: Diagonal Scale Pattern
exercises.description: Play the G major scale diagonally across the fretboard, using 3 notes per string. This creates a smooth ascending path from the low E string at fret 3 to the high E string at fret 15, training fluid position shifts.

notation.title: G Major - 3 Notes Per String Diagonal
notation.staveTitle: G Major Diagonal - 3 Notes Per String

practiceNotes.title: Practice Notes
practiceNotes.text: Three-notes-per-string patterns are excellent for building speed and position shifting simultaneously. Keep your hand relaxed during shifts.

items.title: Building a Mental Map
items: Learn the notes on strings 6 and 5 first - these are your root note references
Use landmark frets (3, 5, 7, 9, 12) as visual guides
Practice finding the same note in multiple octaves across the fretboard
Visualize connecting shapes rather than isolated box patterns

items.title: Smooth Position Shifts
items: Use guide fingers that slide along the string into the new position
Shift during sustained notes so the transition is hidden
Practice shifts with a metronome to keep timing consistent
Look ahead to your target position before you shift
